\subsection*{Simulation Platform: Simulated sensor rig and platform}
\noindent\textbf{8.}\quad \emph{table row:} \texttt{gyr\_n} \textbar{} 0.002 \textbar{} \flag{0.00030--0.00036} \textbar{} rad\,s$^{-1}/\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{9.\ \flag{[Queried]}}\quad The configured gyroscope noise density is \num{2e-3} whereas the stationary
windows of the four recordings give \numrange{3.0e-4}{3.6e-4}, so the
configured value is five to seven times too large. The configured accelerometer
density of 0.02 sits inside the measured spread, but that spread is itself wide,
\numrange{0.015}{0.024} across four recordings of the same simulated sensor.
Both estimators therefore run on an inertial noise model that does not describe
this IMU closely. The bias random walks cannot be checked at all: the longest
stationary interval in any recording is \SI{2.16}{\second} and an
Allan-variance estimate needs minutes. This discrepancy is not incidental: by
the design decision of \reportref{sec:proprio-method} the EKF baseline is run on
these same configured values, so the comparison between the proprioceptive and
visual families is made at a shared handicap rather than at each family's best.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{10.\ \flag{[Queried]}}\quad The accelerometer characterisation is not stable across recordings of the same
simulated sensor. The $x$ bias ranges from \SI{0.013}{} to
\SI{0.079}{\metre\per\second\squared} and the $x$ scale from 1.017 to 1.095
over the four recordings, while the gyroscope $z$ scale agrees to within
\num{0.0007} over the same four. Because the stationary window is between
\SI{1.14}{} and \SI{2.16}{\second} in every case, part of that spread is
estimator variance rather than a property of the sensor, and the accelerometer
terms should not be quoted as calibrated constants.

\medskip

\subsection*{Simulation Platform: Simulation fidelity and its limits}
\noindent\textbf{11.}\quad \emph{table row:} Accelerometer, per axis (\si{\metre\per\second\squared}) \textbar{} \num{0.0566} \textbar{} \num{4.002e-3} \textbar{} \flag{\numrange{1.5e-2}{2.4e-2}} \textbar{} \num{2.00e-3}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{12.}\quad \emph{table row:} \repo{slip1}, \repo{slip2} \textbar{} 0 on all grounds \textbar{} \flag{an ODE feature;
  \repo{dartsim} does not implement it, so inert at any value}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{13.\ \flag{[Threat to validity]}}\quad This is a bias with a known direction. The EKF baseline of
\reportref{sec:results-proprio} is evaluated on a floor where the wheels effectively
cannot slip and with an encoder of unlimited resolution, which is dead
reckoning's best case. Both idealisations favour the proprioceptive estimators
over the visual ones, and neither has been relaxed. Any conclusion that a
wheel-plus-IMU filter matches or beats the visual pipelines should be read as
holding \emph{under these conditions}, not as a general result.
\repo{script/make_slippery_floor.py} generates ground models at a chosen
friction coefficient so that traction can be made an experimental factor, and
\repo{script/encoder_sim.py} imposes a realistic quantisation floor. Neither has
been used in any result reported here.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{14.}\quad \emph{table row:} \repo{gyr_w} \textbar{} \num{0.0001} \textbar{} \num{1.735e-6} \textbar{} \flag{\num{58}$\times$} \textbar{} gyroscope bias random walk

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{15.\ \flag{[Retired evidence for the inflated setting]}}\quad The inflated configuration is retained for every result in this report, on the
strength of an experiment that is no longer part of the reported campaign: in
September 2026 both estimators were re-run on configurations carrying the true
injected densities, and although accuracy improved wherever a run completed,
three of ten runs diverged outright where the inflated configuration diverged in
none. That evidence was recorded on recordings retired on 6 November 2026, so it
is reported here as the reason for a setting rather than as a result, and the
comparison has not been repeated on the current recordings.

\medskip

\subsection*{Simulation Platform: Realistic logistics layouts}
\noindent\textbf{16.}\quad \flag{The generator reproduces the U world exactly but no longer
reproduces the I world: it would now emit eight dock-line items instead of
thirteen and two more clutter instances. The committed world file is the
recorded environment and is the source of these counts.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{17.\ \flag{[Visual verification]}}\quad The generator-side checks are complete, and the first Gazebo session on
6 October 2026 found and fixed one defect the checks could not see (a jack
setting its load down and then stopping on the neighbouring cell, because the
drop command carried one angle for both the parked load and the approach
heading). Three things remain to be confirmed by eye in the simulator rather
than by the checker: that the loads ride on the fork side of the jack, the
shading of the generated door, trailer and yard meshes, and the open/closed
state of each door. Until then the worlds are \status{implemented} in geometry
and \status{partial} in visual verification.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{18.\ \flag{[Provenance]}}\quad None of the six recordings carries a run manifest of its own: the world each
was recorded in is known from the manifests of the replays made on it, not
from the recording. Those manifests agree, and the object inventory each bag
reports is consistent with the layout they name, but a recording whose world
is attested only by later use is weaker evidence than one that records its own
world. A manifest should be written at record time, not at replay time.

\section*{Chapter 4 --- Experiments and Results}

\subsection*{Experiment 1: Estimator Comparison Against a Non-Visual Baseline: Simulation}
\noindent\textbf{1.}\quad \slotstatus{completed}{Four \repo{dataset_allsensor_realistic} recordings, two
layouts each recorded without and with warehouse traffic. Two families of
estimator are scored over the full common interval of each: the non-visual
ones --- wheel odometry, IMU dead reckoning, an EKF at the visual systems' own
inertial noise configuration and a measured-noise EKF as diagnostic --- and
the visual ones, VINS-Fusion once per recording and ORB-SLAM3 with a CPU or
GPU feature extractor and its loop closer active or disabled. Traffic is noted
as a condition, not tested as a factor. The latency and resource measurement
is taken from eighteen repeated runs on the two mapping recordings, three
repeats of each of six configurations, and those repeats are the only
within-configuration spread the campaign measures.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{2.}\quad VINS-Fusion carries a
smaller signature of the same kind, pitch and roll RMS of \SI{1.05}{} and
\SI{1.33}{\degree} against a yaw RMS of \SI{0.24}{\degree}; \flag{whether that is a residual gravity error or the rigid fit absorbing a
tilt has not been separated, and it is reported as an observation.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{3.\ \flag{[Confound: run order]}}\quad The six GPU runs were made consecutively
from 21:04 to 22:04 and the six CPU runs from 23:27 to 00:18, so the
I-recording GPU repeats were the fourth to sixth GPU runs of a session on a
laptop that throttles at \SI{90}{\celsius}; the front-end record notes that
timing comparisons need a cool-start, interleaved order. The six VINS-Fusion
runs are a separate session of 7 November and are not a control for that
state. The U-recording figures are the ones to quote until the I recording is
repeated interleaved.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{4.\ \flag{[Resolved: \repo{realistic_002/loopclosing_gpu}]}}\quad Earlier on 6 November this run was reported as closure-free from its
\repo{loop_closing.csv} and queried. Its manifest shows the real cause: it was
launched on the \repo{realistic_003} bag with \repo{realistic_002}'s output
path, so it was scored against the wrong truth (\SI{4.94}{\metre},
\SI{48.9}{\degree}, 139\,\% of the recording's frames processed). It is set
aside, not deleted; the configuration was re-run on the right bag the same
evening and every table here carries that run.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{5.\ \flag{[Open: the false closure is diagnosed from its correction, not from the images]}}\quad The \SI{14}{\metre} correction and the one-aisle keyframe separation identify
the \repo{realistic_001} closure as false, and both front ends agree; the
matched image pair has not been inspected, and the two April-style guards
that would catch it (a covisibility-consistency window, or a maximum
correction against the inertial drift bound) are untested. Until one is, the
finding is a diagnosis, not a fix.

\medskip

\subsection*{Experiment 1: Estimator Comparison Against a Non-Visual Baseline: Real robot}
\noindent\textbf{6.}\quad \slotstatus{partial}{Four real recordings with an independent planar reference
(\repo{dataset_realv6_000}, \repo{dataset_realv7_000} to \repo{_002}). A
non-visual baseline exists: wheel+gyro dead reckoning with the feedback speed
scaled by a factor fitted once against the tracker on \repo{realv7_000} and
held on the other three. The visual arm is ORB-SLAM3 in four configurations on
each recording, sixteen runs, all made with the fork's patch-15
initialisation switches and scored with no repair applied; they give
\SIrange{0.404}{0.480}{\metre} on \repo{realv6_000},
\SIrange{0.251}{0.268}{} on \repo{realv7_000}, \SIrange{0.442}{1.278}{} on
\repo{_001} and \SIrange{0.172}{0.198}{} on \repo{_002}. Across the held
recordings the two families are in the same accuracy class, the baseline
leading on one, tying on one and losing the third. The EKF of the simulation
slot cannot be formed, because the rig publishes no steering measurement;
VINS-Fusion has no valid run on any recording; and every value is provisional
until the marker-to-IMU lever arm is measured.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{7.\ \flag{[Open: the realv6 scale]}}\quad On \repo{realv6_000} the path-length ratio gives $k=0.43$ where the three
\repo{realv7} bags give $0.32$ to $0.33$, yet the held $k=0.325$ scores a path
ratio of 1.04 on the matched samples. The export is at \SI{1.7}{\hertz} and
fails the validity rules, and the recording predates \repo{realv7} by three
days; whether the firmware unit changed or the sparse export misstates the
path length is not decided, and the \repo{realv6} row is a diagnostic.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{8.\ \flag{[Open: what the improvement is owed to]}}\quad Two things differ between the two sets of runs, not one. Patch 15 is the
first; the second is that \repo{IMU.NoiseGyro} and \repo{IMU.NoiseAcc} were
inflated tenfold on 3 November, and no artefact records which values that
afternoon's runs used, because \repo{run_metadata.csv} stores the
configuration's path and not its contents. The loss of the tilt is
patch 15's: the upstream rule tests keyframe spacing below \SI{2}{\centi\metre}
within \SI{10}{\second} and cannot be influenced by an inertial noise density.
Any part of the accuracy difference is not separable on the present evidence.
One control run, the same bag at today's noise with both switches returned to
upstream, would separate them and has not been made.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{9.\ \flag{[Provenance: the 3 November estimates are gone]}}\quad The re-runs overwrote \path{output/output_orb/real/dataset_realv7_00*/} in
place, so the pre-patch-15 estimates of all three recordings no longer exist
and neither \reportref{tab:realv7-tilt} nor \reportref{fig:realv7-tilt} can be
regenerated; the frozen copies beside the generator are the only record of the
behaviour this section reports as corrected. A run directory should be
written under a name that carries its configuration, so that a re-run cannot
overwrite the evidence for the behaviour it replaces.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{10.\ \flag{[Sparse reference]}}\quad The tracker ran at \SI{1.7}{\hertz} rather than its nominal \SI{7}{\hertz} on
\repo{realv6}, and
the validity rules were written for the faster export. Either the export has to
be re-captured at full rate or a rule for sparse references has to be written
before any value from this recording is quoted outside a diagnostic.

\medskip

\subsection*{Experiment 2: Offline YOLO Detector Performance: Simulation}
\noindent\textbf{11.}\quad \slotstatus{completed}{Four realistic-warehouse recordings, 12\,698 left-camera
frames, scored on 7 November 2026 against projected simulator ground truth
with the four-class checkpoint
(\repo{weight/runs_1/detect/train/weights/best.pt}: bin, box, bucket,
forklift), whose fourth class fires on the pallet jacks that are the moving
objects of these recordings. Pooled precision 0.747; recall 0.502 over the
truth boxes the exemptions keep and 0.288 over every truth box;
moving-object recall 0.288. The walking people are simulator actors with no
pose and no class, so they are outside the score on both sides.}

\medskip

\noindent\textbf{12.}\quad \slotstatus{planned}{Real imagery exists; no real ground-truth boxes do.}

\subsection*{Experiment 3: Dense Map Reconstruction and Map-Quality Evaluation: Simulation}
\noindent\textbf{13.}\quad \slotstatus{partial}{Five databases are scored for geometry and drivability:
the tiny warehouse, which passes, and four realistic-warehouse maps --- two
mapping recordings, one per layout, each built closure-free under two
back-end configurations, A and B --- all of which fail the quality
criterion fixed before scoring. The tiny map's independent drivability
reference remains lost.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{14.\ \flag{[Queried: reproducibility of the drivability half]}}\quad The geometry result is fully reproducible: both \repo{map/map_tiny.db} and the
world file are present. The drivability result is not. Its reference run,
\repo{dataset_static_tiny_repeat}, is absent from \repo{dataset/} and from the
removable drive, and the only surviving recording of this warehouse is the one
that built the map, which would answer a weaker question
(\reportref{sec:map-drivability}). The database additionally stores an empty parameter
set, so the configuration that produced it is not recoverable from the file, and
the RTAB-Map engineering record's claim that the node stamps match no dataset is
contradicted by the pose agreement reported above. The drivability figures should
therefore be read as a dated measurement rather than a standing result, and should
not be carried into the major report until an independent route has been recorded
and retained.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{15.}\quad The failure was attributed there to the front end under repeated
structure, not to the mapping back end. \flag{No database, run directory or figure for this attempt is registered in
the repository at the cutoff, so the result is reported on the strength of the
progress record and cannot be audited. A database identified from its contents
as this attempt (18 nodes, \SI{37}{\metre} along one aisle, poses leaving the
floor, placeable in no large world) was found among the unregistered
databases on 22 October 2026 and deleted with them on 6 November, unscored.
The attempt must be repeated with its artifacts retained before it is carried
into any conclusion.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{16.\ \flag{[Queried: front end of the realistic builds]}}\quad RTAB-Map took its pose from TF, so the odometry came from whichever front end
was running; none of the four databases records which, and the build Bs
were made during the latency sessions of Experiment~3, whose load on the front
end is not recorded either. The precision loss cannot be placed on the front
end against the back end, nor the November drop on parameters against session,
until the build manifest names both.

\medskip

\noindent\textbf{17.}\quad \slotstatus{planned}{No RTAB-Map database has been built from real imagery, and
no reference geometry of the site exists to score one against.}

\medskip

\subsection*{Experiment 4: Autonomous Navigation on the Reconstructed Map: Simulation}
\noindent\textbf{18.}\quad \slotstatus{partial}{Seven live runs on 12 November 2026, in three of the four
worlds, measure the localisation against ground truth over hand-driven routes
of \SIrange{21}{153}{\metre}. No goal was commanded in any of them, so the
goal-reaching measures of the reporting rules below are still unused and that
half of the experiment remains \status{planned}. The protocol, goal set and
success criteria are now fixed in code (\repo{script/exp4_protocol.yaml},
generated by \repo{script/exp4_goals.py}), which is what the previous revision
of this document recorded as missing.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{19.}\quad The ground truth
reports the model origin and every estimate reports the camera/IMU body, so the
\SI{0.338}{\metre} lever arm is applied to the ground truth before the fit and
before any comparison, and never to recorded data. \flag{An earlier revision fitted against the uncorrected ground truth and
reported the resulting \SI{0.337}{\metre} residual as confirmation that the fit
was right, on the grounds that it equalled the lever arm. That was the bias, not
the evidence: a rigid transform cannot absorb an offset that rotates with the
body, so it absorbed part of it as translation and left the rest as residual.}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{20.}\quad \textbf{Reporting rules, goal-reaching.} \flag{Fixed before any run exists,
so that the result cannot be chosen after the fact, and left unchanged here.} A
goal counts as reached when the base frame is within \SI{0.25}{\metre} and
\SI{10}{\degree} of it and the planner reports success.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{21.}\quad \textbf{Reporting rules, pose tracking.} \flag{Defined after these data
existed, and reported as the weaker claim it is.} Error is the planar distance
between the published \texttt{map}~$\rightarrow$~\texttt{base\_link} transform,
sampled at \SI{2}{\hertz}, and the lever-arm-corrected ground truth
interpolated to the same instants.

\medskip
